candidates.label: Incomplete Kawasaki disease with right coronary artery dilation, complicated by plastic bronchitis, triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection
missing_or_uncertain: Fever duration >5 days not clearly documented
Mucocutaneous findings (rash, conjunctivitis, oral changes) not reported
Echocardiography done only on day 28, no earlier baseline

candidates.label: Severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia with plastic bronchitis and systemic complications including coronary arteritis and hepatic dysfunction
missing_or_uncertain: Coronary artery dilation is not a typical complication of M. pneumoniae infection
Recurrent fever without infection on day 28 not explained

candidates.label: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with coronary artery dilation, associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-infection
missing_or_uncertain: No evidence of COVID-19 exposure or testing
Clinical features overlap with Kawasaki disease; MIS-C typically requires SARS-CoV-2 association

candidates.label: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia with plastic bronchitis and reactive airway disease, complicated by sepsis-related coronary dilation and liver injury
missing_or_uncertain: Sepsis does not typically cause coronary artery dilation
Recurrent fever on day 28 without infection manifestations is not explained

candidates.label: Primary systemic vasculitis (e.g., polyarteritis nodosa) with pulmonary and cardiac involvement, triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection
missing_or_uncertain: Vasculitis is rare in a 6-year-old and would require more evidence of systemic involvement
Plastic bronchitis and confirmed M. pneumoniae point more to an infectious trigger

response.rationale: The presence of right coronary artery dilation on echocardiography (F10) is a hallmark of Kawasaki disease, especially when combined with recurrent fever (F09) and elevated liver enzymes (F11). The confirmed M. pneumoniae infection (F05, F08) and plastic bronchitis (F07) support an infectious trigger for Kawasaki disease. Incomplete Kawasaki is favored because typical mucocutaneous findings are not reported. D2 (severe mycoplasma pneumonia) is less likely because coronary artery dilation is not a typical complication of mycoplasma infection. The recurrent fever without infection on day 28 and the coronary dilation specifically point to Kawasaki disease. Other differentials (MIS-C, vasculitis) are less supported by the available evidence.
